title: Names and generic extensions

based_on.title: Forcing Summer School Lecture Notes
based_on.pages: 27–30 (§10.1, names, evaluation and structural properties; section by Justin Palumbo; revised 2014-09-06)

based_on.title: Set Theory
based_on.pages: 99–100 (names, generic extensions and elementary properties; revision 2026-01-31)

summary: Evaluate ground-model names to obtain a transitive extension containing the old sets and the filter, with the same ordinals and explicit names for pairs, unions, and a Cohen sequence.
abstract: A generic filter can add a new set, and adjoining it should also supply sets built from it. Names encode these possible sets before the filter is known: each prospective member carries a condition, and evaluation keeps the members whose conditions belong to the filter. For a transitive ground model of ZFC, values of its names form a transitive extension containing every old set and the filter itself. Explicit names produce exact pairs and unions, and name ranks show that no ordinals are added. These facts already hold for any filter; for a Cohen generic, an explicit name additionally places the new binary sequence inside the extension.
